policy_name: Fixed Time Period Admissions for F, J, and I Nonimmigrants
affected_groups: I representatives of foreign information media
current_policy: Admitted for 'duration of status' (D/S), an unspecified admission period as long as complying with the classification.
proposed_change: Replace duration of status (D/S) with admissions for a fixed time period requiring nonimmigrants to apply to DHS for extensions of stay (EOS) if they want to stay beyond the fixed period.
plain_english: Instead of staying in the U.S. as long as they follow the rules (D/S), F, J, and most I visa holders will get a fixed period to stay and must apply to extend their stay if needed.
allowed: Employment authorization extensions under certain conditions
restricted_or_prohibited: Indefinite stays based on D/S framework
Staying beyond authorized period without EOS approval
exceptions: I nonimmigrants from People's Republic of China have a limited 90-day time period admission
time_limits_or_durations: Admissions for F and J limited up to 4 years
I nonimmigrants limited up to 240 days, except for some from PRC with up to 90 days
30-day preparation to depart after course completion (F-1)
Up to 240 days employment authorization extension while EOS pending
evidence_quote: DHS proposes to amend its regulations by changing the admission period in the F, J, and I classifications from duration of status to an admission for a fixed time period...Nonimmigrants who would like to stay in the United States beyond their fixed date of admission would need to apply directly to DHS for an extension of stay (EOS).

policy_name: Revised Extension of Stay (EOS) Application Procedures
current_policy: Extensions granted during D/S status without a formal fixed admission period.
proposed_change: Outline a specific process for EOS applications for F, J, and I nonimmigrants including biometric collection requirements and automatic employment authorization extensions up to 240 days for F nonimmigrants with timely filed EOS applications.
plain_english: Nonimmigrants will apply for stay extensions with clear steps including providing biometrics; students can keep working up to 240 days if their extension is pending.
allowed: Auto-extension of employment authorization up to 240 days for F nonimmigrants under economic hardship
Employment continuation for J-1 and I nonimmigrants while EOS pending
restricted_or_prohibited: Employment authorization expiration ends work authorization for J-2 dependents once EAD expires
exceptions: I nonimmigrants from PRC have special provisions related to admission length and EOS
time_limits_or_durations: Auto-extension of EAD up to 240 days or regulatory notice period
EOS application period aligned with fixed admission periods
evidence_quote: Outlining the process for EOS applications for F, J, and I nonimmigrants; ...Providing for collection of biometric information in conjunction with an EOS application for F, J, and I nonimmigrants as may be required by 8 CFR 103.16; ...Allowing F nonimmigrants whose timely filed EOS applications remain pending ... to receive an auto-extension of their current authorization for on-campus and off-campus employment based on severe economic hardship resulting from emergent circumstances under existing 8 CFR 214.2(f)(5)(v).

policy_name: Limits on Educational Program Changes and Stay Durations in F-1 Status
current_policy: Students admitted under D/S with flexibility to change programs; language training students have less clear aggregate limits.
proposed_change: Require F-1 students to complete their first academic year at the initial school before transferring unless SEVP authorizes an exception; prohibit graduate students from changing programs during study; restrict changes to same or lower educational level; limit language training students to 24 months aggregate stay; reduce allowed departure preparation period from 60 to 30 days after completion of study or training.
plain_english: F-1 students must stay one academic year before transferring schools, can't change graduate programs mid-study, can't move to equal or lower levels once a program is completed, language students limited to 2 years total, and must leave within 30 days after finishing studies.
allowed: One academic year minimum before transfer (with exceptions)
Change to higher educational level programs only after program completion
restricted_or_prohibited: Graduate level students prohibited from changing programs mid-course
Reducing departure preparation time to 30 days
Language training limited to 24 months total
time_limits_or_durations: 24-month aggregate limit for language training students including breaks
30 days to prepare to depart after course or training completion
evidence_quote: For F–1 students changing educational objectives or transferring to an SEVP-certified school, requiring that the student complete his or her first academic year ... unless an exception is authorized by SEVP; Prohibiting F–1 students at the graduate education level from changing programs at any point during a program of study; ...Limiting language training students to an aggregate 24-month period of stay, including breaks and an annual vacation; Decreasing from 60 to 30 days the allowed period for F–1 nonimmigrants to prepare to depart from the United States after completion of a course of study or authorized period of post-completion practical training.

policy_name: Clarification and Codification of I Nonimmigrant Status Requirements
current_policy: I status granted for duration of foreign employment duties without fixed end date apart from some PRC exceptions; ambiguous definitions and evidence requirements.
proposed_change: Replace D/S with fixed time period admissions for I nonimmigrants not exceeding 240 days (except some PRC nationals with 90 days); codify definition of foreign media organizations consistent with existing USCIS and DOS practice; update evidence required for I nonimmigrant eligibility; clarify continued work authorization during EOS pendency for I nonimmigrants under 8 CFR 274a.12(b)(20).
plain_english: I visa holders get set stay times up to 240 days and must reapply if extended. DHS defines foreign media groups clearly and specifies what documents are needed. I visa holders can keep working if their extension is being processed.
allowed: Working for foreign employer during EOS pendency up to 240 days
Admission periods up to 240 days for I nonimmigrants
restricted_or_prohibited: Admission lasting longer than 240 days without extension
D/S admissions for I nonimmigrants replaced
exceptions: I nonimmigrants from PRC limited to 90-day fixed admission period
time_limits_or_durations: 240 days maximum admission period generally; 90 days for some PRC nationals
evidence_quote: Replacing D/S for I nonimmigrants with admission for a fixed time period until they complete the activities or assignments consistent with the I classification, not to exceed 240 days (with the exception of some I aliens from the People’s Republic of China), with an EOS available for I nonimmigrants who can meet specified EOS requirements; Codifying the definition of a foreign media organization for I nonimmigrant status, consistent with long-standing USCIS and U.S. Department of State (DOS) practice; Clarifying that I nonimmigrants are authorized to continue working in the United States for their foreign employer, under 8 CFR 274a.12(b)(20), while their timely filed EOS application is pending for up to 240 days.

policy_name: Change of Status Application Abandonment upon Departure
affected_groups: F and J nonimmigrants applying for change of status
current_policy: Policy on abandonment of change of status applications when alien departs is not codified.
proposed_change: Codify policy that DHS deems an application to change nonimmigrant status, including change to F or J status, abandoned if the alien departs the United States while the application is pending.
plain_english: If a person applies to change their visa status and leaves the U.S. before a decision, their application is considered abandoned.
restricted_or_prohibited: Change of status application remains pending only if alien stays in U.S.; departing abandons application.
evidence_quote: Codifying the long-standing policy under which DHS deems abandoned an application to change to another nonimmigrant status, including F or J status, if the alien who timely filed the application departs the United States while the application is pending.
